To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ATRX directs PRC2 to the Xi by binding to Xist RNA; that this binding is mediated by a novel ATRX domain, termed the Xist RNA-binding domain (XRBD), which is distinct from the ATPase domain; that ATRX and PRC2 are recruited together to other polycomb targets in cis and in trans, and that ATRX is required for the recruitment of PRC2 at these targets.
ATRX binds Xist RNA and PRC2 and that ATRX is required for PRC2 binding to its targets, including Xist RNA and other X-linked genes.

(1) ATRX is recruited to the Xi by its interaction with XIST, (2) the ATRX–XIST interaction is necessary for the localization and activity of PRC2, and (3) the ATRXA–XIST complex binds to the promoters of a subset of Polycomb targets, including the Hox cluster.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying X chromosome dosage compensation in female mammals, which involves the transcriptional silencing of one of the two X chromosomes in somatic cells.
the role of ATRX in the recruitment of PRC2 and H3K27me3 to Xist RNA.
how the ATRX protein, which contains an ATPase/helicase domain, binds to the Xist RNA and directs binding of the PRC2 complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ATRX and macroH2A are two different proteins that have been shown to bind to Xist RNA.
ATRX binds to macroH2a on the inactive X and is required for the recruitment of PRC2.
‘‘The ATRX helicase, which binds macroH2A and is recruited to Xist RNA, is required for X inactivation’’ (Ratnakumar et al., 2009).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ATRX directs the recruitment of PRC2 onto Xist RNA and polycomb targets, but not to H3K9me3 targets, by binding to the H2A.Z-containing nucleosome at the 5′ end of Xist RNA.
ATRX is required for the binding of PRC2 and macroH2A1 at the Xi, and ATRX is also required to maintain the Xist RNA coating of the Xi.
ATRX directs the assembly of PRC2 on Xist RNA and PRC2 targets, and ATRX is recruited to these targets by macroH2A (Ratnakumar et al., 2009; Ratnakumar etal., 2012).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ATRX protein is required for PRC2 recruitment to the inactive X chromosome, and this function is independent of its ATPase activity.
ATRX is an important component of the Xist RNA–PRC2 complex and that this complex is essential for X inactivation.
ATRX and PRC2 are required to recruit macroH2A to Xist RNA.
